component.name: psd.ai
component.summary: Local-first AI assistant with an offline model group, voice and desktop control

description.p: psd.ai runs entirely on your own machine. On first launch it measures your RAM, VRAM and CPU, picks a group of three to five hardware-fit GGUF models, downloads the llama.cpp server for your GPU backend (CUDA, Vulkan, SYCL or CPU) and serves one model per port — so the chat model, a coding model and a fast utility model are all resident at once.

Mixture-of-experts models are placed deliberately: attention and shared weights stay on the GPU while experts spill into RAM, which lets a mid-range card host a far larger model than a VRAM-only planner would allow. Vision models load their projector so the assistant can read screenshots and documents.

ul.li: Offline chat with a locally served model group — no API key required
Voice mode ("Talk to psd.ai") with on-device Whisper transcription
Jarvis: screen reading, window control, typing and clipboard, Wayland-first with an X11 fallback
Research, email, calendar and file tools the agent can call
Power profiles: balanced, power, or max (one huge model instead of a group)

description.p: Built for Fedora: dependencies come from dnf, the engine can run as a systemd user unit, and SELinux stays Enforcing.

ul.li: 2026 local model catalogue with MoE-aware GPU/RAM placement
Linux llama.cpp assets (.tar.gz) with per-backend selection and cudart companions
Wayland PC control through ydotool/wtype/grim and the XDG Desktop Portal
dnf-based setup, systemd user unit, RPM packaging
